symbols.name: path start vertex
symbols.meaning: The first vertex of the three-vertex path, where the route starts.
symbols.quote: Take a path of three vertices $v_0$, $v_1$, $v_2$, and write $D_{v_0}$, $D_{v_1}$, $D_{v_2}$ for the frames at them.

symbols.name: path middle vertex
symbols.meaning: The middle vertex of the three-vertex path, whose frame cancels in the composed change.
symbols.quote: Take a path of three vertices $v_0$, $v_1$, $v_2$, and write $D_{v_0}$, $D_{v_1}$, $D_{v_2}$ for the frames at them.

symbols.name: path end vertex
symbols.meaning: The last vertex of the three-vertex path, where the route ends.
symbols.quote: Take a path of three vertices $v_0$, $v_1$, $v_2$, and write $D_{v_0}$, $D_{v_1}$, $D_{v_2}$ for the frames at them.

relations.quote: The endpoint operator is realised by a [linear network](linear-network-frames.md) on each role array once all intermediate frames have cancelled, so it depends only on the frames at the two ends of a route.
The endpoint operator is instantiated by the [bit procedure](bit-procedure.md) as an [address shear](address-shear.md): a map that adds one address field to the other and leaves the second unchanged.
The endpoint operator maps the stored form of the [logical array](logical-array.md) $g$ at the start of the route to its stored form at the end.
The endpoint operator holds on every role of the [scalar network](subset-intersection-network.md), including the roles that carry auxiliary scalar values.
That shear is implemented by a small number of [field interchanges](address-interchange.md).
